extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology (readers of a homotopy theory textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook exposition of parts of homotopy theory: excision-type statements for relative homotopy, quasiﬁbrations and criteria to recognize them, symmetric products and the Dold–Thom theorem, and the basic properties/axioms of Steenrod squares and powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excisive triad (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An excisive triad is a space X with subspaces A and B such that X is the union of the interiors of A and B; in this situation we call (X; A, B) an excisive triad. By a map f : (X; A, B)→(Y; C, D) we mean f : X→Y with f(A) ⊂ C and f(B) ⊂ D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the hypothesis context for Proposition 4K.1 and other excision-style arguments. The explicit interior-union condition is important: excision for homology is trivial under this condition, but excision fails for homotopy groups so hypotheses must be checked carefully. Example: take preimages of hemisphere covers under a quotient map to exhibit failure when hypotheses omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4K.1 hypothesis/conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f : (X; A, B)→(Y; C, D) be a map of excisive triads. If the induced maps πi(A, A ∩ B)→πi(C, C ∩ D) and πi(B, A ∩ B)→πi(D, C ∩ D) are bijections for i < n and surjections for i = n, for all choices of basepoints, then the same is true of the induced maps πi(X, A)→πi(Y, C). By symmetry the conclusion holds also for the maps πi(X, B)→πi(Y, D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the homotopy analogue of the excision-isomorphism idea for homology, but it requires strong hypotheses on the corner pairs (A,A∩B) and (B,A∩B). The proof reduces to an inclusion case (via mapping cylinders) and uses the equivalence of several extension/injectivity/surjectivity conditions for relative homotopy groups. Beware that excision can fail for homotopy (the text gives an explicit counterexample using collapsing ∂D2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of three extension/injectivity/surjectivity conditions for relative homotopy
rubrics_metrics.description: For an inclusion (X,A) ↪ (Y,C) and each n ≥ 1 the following are equivalent: (i) for all basepoints the map πi(X,A)→πi(Y,C) induced by inclusion is surjective for i = n and has trivial kernel for i = n−1; (ii) every map (Dn × {0} ∪ ∂+Dn × I, ∂−Dn × {0} ∪ S^{n−2}×I)→(Y,C) taking (∂+Dn × {1}, S^{n−2}×{1}) to (X,A) extends to (Dn × I, ∂−Dn × I)→(Y,C) taking (Dn × {1}, ∂−Dn × {1}) to (X,A); (iii) same as (ii) with the restriction to ∂+Dn × I independent of the I-coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalent formulations give practical extension/homotopy criteria to check surjectivity and injectivity behavior of relative homotopy maps. The proof shows (ii)↔(iii) and uses (iii)⇒(i) and (i)⇒(ii) by explicit extension/homotopy constructions involving hemispheres, small disks, and pushing in collars. Use these formulations when constructing or obstructing relative homotopy extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 4K.2 (local-to-global weak homotopy equivalence via covers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a map f : X→Y and open covers {Ui} of X and {Vi} of Y with f(Ui) ⊂ Vi for all i, then if each restriction f : Ui→Vi and more generally each f : Ui1 ∩ ··· ∩ Uin → Vi1 ∩ ··· ∩ Vin is a weak homotopy equivalence, so is f : X→Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the five-lemma and Proposition 4K.1 to bootstrap from local relative π-isomorphisms to global ones; reduce finite and then infinite covers via compactness of images of spheres. Practical guideline: check weak equivalence on all finite intersections of the cover to deduce global weak equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of quasifibration (two equivalent forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map p : E→B with B path-connected is a quasifibration if the induced map p_* : πi(E, p^{-1}(b), x0)→πi(B, b) is an isomorphism for all b ∈ B, x0 ∈ p^{-1}(b), and i ≥ 0. An equivalent condition: the inclusion of each fiber p^{-1}(b) into the homotopy fiber F_b of p over b is a weak homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasifibrations generalize fibrations in the sense that they induce the correct long exact sequence of homotopy groups even without the full homotopy lifting property. Check either the π-isomorphism condition or fiber→homotopy-fiber weak equivalence. Note: for non-path-connected bases there is an extended definition (exercise 5) involving π0 exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4K.3: sufficient conditions for quasifibration
rubrics_metrics.description: A map p : E→B is a quasifibration if any one of the following conditions is satisfied: (a) B is union of open sets V1,V2 such that each restriction p^{-1}(V1)→V1, p^{-1}(V2)→V2, and p^{-1}(V1∩V2)→V1∩V2 is a quasifibration; (b) B is union of an increasing sequence B1⊂B2⊂··· with each compact set lying in some Bn and each restriction p^{-1}(Bn)→Bn is a quasifibration; (c) there is a deformation F_t of E into E' covering a deformation of B into B' such that E'→B' is a quasifibration and F1 : p^{-1}(b)→p^{-1}(F1(b)) is a weak homotopy equivalence for each b∈B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use (a) to glue quasifibrations on an open cover, (b) to handle filtered unions and locally-compact-type arguments, and (c) to reduce to a subspace via a deformation. The proof sketches indicate handling π0 issues by assuming path-connected fibers or referring to the exercise for the general case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric product SP_n(X) and SP(X) (definition and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a space X the n-fold symmetric product SP_n(X) is the quotient of X^n by the action of the symmetric group permuting factors. With a basepoint e∈X the inclusions SP_n(X) ↪ SP_{n+1}(X) induced by (x1,…,xn)↦(x1,…,xn,e) give SP(X) as the union (direct limit). SP_n and SP are homotopy functors: f:X→Y induces f_*:SP_n(X)→SP_n(Y), and homotopic maps induce homotopic induced maps. For simplicial complexes there is a natural CW/simplicial structure on SP_n(X) and SP(X) (via barycentric subdivisions) and the CW topology is used for further arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key practical consequences: SP preserves homotopy equivalences (for connected CW complexes), SP(S^2)≈CP^∞ and SP(S^1)≃S^1 are useful examples. Beware that the product topology definition and the CW topology may differ, but they have the same compact sets and the CW topology is adopted here. Building CW/simplicial structures on symmetric products is nontrivial but canonical for simplicial complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4K.6 (Dold–Thom theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor X ↦ π_i SP(X) for i ≥ 1 coincides with the functor X ↦ H_i(X; Z) on the category of basepointed connected CW complexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: SP(X) has weak homotopy type of product of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces (K(H_n(X),n)); in particular SP(S^n) is a K(Z,n). The proof strategy is to show SP(A)→SP(X)→SP(X/A) is a quasifibration to obtain long exact sequences in homotopy and then check homology axioms to identify the homology theory given by π_* SP(X) with ordinary homology with Z coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 4K.7 (H–space consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A path-connected, commutative, associative H–space with a strict identity element has the weak homotopy type of a product of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to SP(X): since SP(X) is a commutative associative H–space with strict identity, its weak homotopy type is constrained to be a product ∏ K(H_n(X),n). The corollary follows from constructing maps M(G_n,n)→X inducing π_n isomorphisms and assembling these via the H–space structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy to prove projection SP(X)→SP(X/A) is a quasifibration (filtration method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p:SP(X)→SP(X/A). Define B_n = SP_n(X/A) and E_n = p^{-1}(B_n) (points in SP(X) with at most n coordinates in X−A). By Lemma 4K.3(b) it suffices to show p:E_n→B_n is a quasifibration for each n, proved by induction: show p is a quasifibration over a neighborhood of B_{n−1} (using a deformation F_t and Lemma 4K.3(c)) and over B_n−B_{n−1}, then apply Lemma 4K.3(a) to glue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key technical ingredients: replace (X,A) by the mapping cylinder so X−A is path-connected, define a neighborhood U of E_{n−1} in E_n consisting of points with at least one coordinate in a neighborhood N of A, induce deformations Ft, and check F1 induces weak equivalences on fibers. For B_n−B_{n−1} identify it with SP_n(X−A) where a section exists, and use elementary homotopy arguments to show π_*-injectivity/surjectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the induced map π_i(X)→π_i SP(X) as the Hurewicz homomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: The map π_i(X)→π_i SP(X) = H_i(X; Z) induced by the inclusion X = SP_1(X) ↪ SP(X) is the Hurewicz homomorphism. The identification reduces to checking the case X=S^i (and ultimately i=1) where the inclusion induces an isomorphism on π_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation ties the Dold–Thom identification to classical Hurewicz theory and explains why the constructed homology groups hi(X)=π_i SP(X) recover ordinary homology with Z coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4L.1 (classification of cohomology operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed m,n,G,H there is a bijection between the set of all cohomology operations Θ: H^m(X;G)→H^n(X;H) and H^n(K(G,m);H), defined by Θ ↦ Θ(ι) where ι∈H^m(K(G,m);G) is a fundamental class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a convenient way to characterize and construct natural transformations between cohomology functors: pick a class in H^n of the appropriate Eilenberg–MacLane space. Consequences: operations that decrease dimension are trivial and operations that preserve dimension correspond to coefficient homomorphisms (since H^m(K(G,m);H)≈Hom(G,H)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Axioms/properties of Steenrod squares (Sqi)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Steenrod squares Sqi: H^n(X;Z2)→H^{n+i}(X;Z2), i≥0, satisfy: (1) naturality Sqi(f^*(α))=f^*(Sqi(α)); (2) additivity Sqi(α+β)=Sqi(α)+Sqi(β); (3) Cartan formula Sqi(α∪β)=∑_j Sq^j(α)∪Sq^{i−j}(β); (4) stability Sqi(σ(α))=σ(Sqi(α)) under suspension σ: H^n→H^{n+1}(ΣX); (5) Sqi(α)=α^2 if i=|α| and Sqi(α)=0 if i>|α|; (6) Sq^0 = 1 (identity); (7) Sq^1 is the Z2 Bockstein β associated to 0→Z2→Z4→Z2→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the basic axioms used in applications; (5) shows squares extend cup-square; (4) stability makes them usable in stable homotopy arguments (e.g., detecting nontrivial stable homotopy via Hopf invariant 1 theorem). The Cartan formula controls behavior on products. Note the relationship Sq^{2i+1}=Sq^1 Sq^{2i}=β Sq^{2i} (Adem relations discussed later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Axioms/properties of Steenrod powers (P_i) for odd primes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Steenrod power operations P_i: H^n(X;Z_p)→H^{n+2i(p−1)}(X;Z_p) (p odd) satisfy: (1) naturality P_i(f^*(α))=f^*(P_i(α)); (2) additivity P_i(α+β)=P_i(α)+P_i(β); (3) Cartan formula P_i(α∪β)=∑_j P_j(α)∪P_{i−j}(β); (4) stability P_i(σ(α))=σ(P_i(α)); (5) germinal property P_i(α)=α^p if 2i=|α|, and P_i(α)=0 if 2i>|α|; (6) P_0 = 1 (identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret P_i as stable analogues of the pth-power cup operation; (5) explains the degree shift 2i(p−1). The Bockstein β is not among the P_i's but interacts with them (and Sq relations for p=2). Adem relations (later) give the algebraic structure among P_i's. These axioms suffice for many applications without constructing the operations explicitly.
